children: Graphite India shares surged nearly 18 percent on Wednesday, September 9, while HEG hit its 5 percent upper circuit, as a sharp graphite electrode price hike announced by US-based GrafTech International fuelled expectations of stronger realisations and margins for Indian manufacturers.

Graphite India stock jumped 17.8 percent to Rs 865 in morning trade, emerging as the top gainer on the BSE Smallcap index and ranking among the most actively traded stocks on both the NSE and BSE. The stock has now gained around 32 percent in 2026, sharply outperforming the Nifty 50, which is down about 10 percent over the same period. The company’s market capitalisation stood at around Rs 16,700 crore.

HEG Advanced Materials shares also rallied, rising 4.99 percent to hit the upper circuit at Rs 271.5. The company commanded a market capitalisation of around Rs 5,233 crore. The gains came against a weak broader market. At 10:15 am, the Sensex was down 606 points, or 0.80 percent, at 74,971, while the Nifty 50 fell 149.5 points, or 0.63 percent, to 23,485.60.

The trigger came from GrafTech International, whose shares surged around 15 percent on Wall Street overnight after the global graphite electrode producer announced a minimum 30 percent increase in graphite electrode prices.

The price increase is effective immediately for all open commercial negotiations and follows an earlier pricing action announced in March. GrafTech said graphite electrode prices have declined considerably over the past three years even as some raw-material, energy and logistics costs have increased, prompting the company to seek a return to more sustainable pricing levels.

The development is being viewed as a positive read-through for Indian graphite electrode manufacturers. According to a CNBC-TV18 report, GrafTech's move could potentially translate into an increase of around $1,500 per tonne in Indian graphite electrode realisations. If sustained, higher realisations could support profitability and margins for domestic producers.

GrafTech's pricing action also follows its recent announcement of a 51,000-tonne reduction in capacity, strengthening expectations of tighter supply conditions in the global graphite electrode market.

Graphite India is currently the only listed pure-play exposure to the graphite electrode business in India. HEG's graphite electrode operations are in the process of being housed in a separately listed company following the group's recent demerger. The existing listed entity, HEG Advanced Materials, retains the advanced materials, battery energy solutions and green power businesses, while HEG Graphite will house the graphite electrode operations and is expected to list separately next month.

Graphite India has an annual graphite electrode manufacturing capacity of 80,000 tonnes, making it the country's largest producer. The company had also reported stronger June-quarter earnings last month. Graphite India's net profit rose 28.4 percent year-on-year to Rs 172 crore in the first quarter, while revenue increased 26.6 percent to Rs 842 crore.
